paragraphs: Graph transformers need to combine information about individual nodes with information about how those nodes connect. Existing approaches introduce graph neural network modules or positional encodings, but the reason these strategies work has remained unclear. This paper identifies a shared mechanism called Cross Aggregation: interactions between graph topology and node attributes help produce useful representations.

The authors use this interpretation to build UGCFormer, a graph transformer framework with linear computational complexity. Its Dual Cross-attention module lets representations of connectivity and node attributes interact as they are learned. The theoretical analysis shows that this module can adaptively capture relationships between these two sources of information.

The framework also includes a consistency constraint that aligns its representations to reduce overfitting associated with having two channels. Evaluations across multiple benchmark datasets support its effectiveness and efficiency. The contribution therefore combines an explanation of existing design choices with an architecture that explicitly builds around the identified interaction.
neurips-2025-a-closer-look-at-graph-tran.tldr: UGCFormer uses interactions between graph structure and node attributes to build an efficient graph transformer with linear computational complexity.

paragraphs: Guiding an entire team of learning agents can become impractical as the system grows. This paper investigates whether intervention on one selected agent can help steer the collective outcome. It uses multi-agent influence diagrams to describe how agents interact and how external guidance enters the system.

The authors distinguish an interaction paradigm, which describes these relationships, from a learning paradigm, which concerns how agents learn. Their targeted interaction paradigm is implemented through Pre-Strategy Intervention, a causal inference technique. Within this framework, maximizing the relevant causal effect can achieve an outcome that combines the main task goal with an additional desired objective.

The diagrams also support a relevance graph analysis for determining whether a learning paradigm is workable under a chosen interaction design. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of targeted intervention and verify the analysis. The approach matters because it supplies both a mechanism for more focused guidance and a formal tool for assessing whether the surrounding learning arrangement can support it.
neurips-2025-a-principle-of-targeted-int.tldr: The paper develops a causal framework for steering cooperative agents through intervention on a single agent.

paragraphs: An attack on a vision-language model does not necessarily produce a meaningful mistake by an embodied agent. If an image becomes too inconsistent with the task instructions, the model may generate an invalid response rather than an actionable decision. This paper identifies that mismatch as a reason some attacks have limited effects on physical interactions.

AdvEDM instead changes the model's perception of a few important objects while preserving the meaning of the rest of the image. This keeps more of the visual scene compatible with the task context. The framework has two variants: AdvEDM-R removes the perceived semantics of a specified object, while AdvEDM-A introduces the semantics of a new object.

The intended result is a decision that remains valid for the task but is incorrect because of altered perception. Experiments in general scenarios and embodied decision-making tasks report fine-grained control and strong attack performance. The findings highlight the safety relevance of selective perceptual errors that can propagate into agent actions.
neurips-2025-advedm-fine-grained-adversa.tldr: AdvEDM selectively alters object perception to induce valid but incorrect decisions in vision-language-based embodied agents.

paragraphs: This benchmark asks language models to write Python programs that compute integer sequences accurately and efficiently. Its focus is algorithmic reasoning: the program must generate the sequence rather than return stored values. The tasks come from 1,000 sequences in the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences, divided into easy and hard categories.

Half the sequences are classical entries and half were added recently, a design intended to reduce training-data contamination. An automated detector flags lookup-table use so that memorized sequence values do not substitute for computation. The authors validate this detector by comparing its judgments with those of human experts.

Evaluations cover models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Google. Reasoning-specialized models achieve substantially higher accuracy than non-reasoning models, particularly on more complex tasks. Nevertheless, performance on the hard sequences remains poor overall. The results show that improved reasoning capabilities help with program synthesis while leaving substantial difficulty in turning demanding mathematical descriptions into reliable algorithms.
neurips-2025-benchmarking-large-language.tldr: A benchmark of 1,000 integer sequences tests algorithmic code generation and finds that hard sequences remain challenging even for reasoning-specialized models.

paragraphs: Low-rank adaptation fine-tunes a language model through a compact set of adjustable weights. Standard LoRA applies the same input-output projection to every token, even though tokens carry different meanings. This paper argues that sharing an identical projection limits how well the adaptation can respond to token-specific information.

TopLoRA makes the adaptation depend on the input token. It retains the two low-rank matrices used by LoRA but inserts a diagonal matrix generated from the current token between them. This token-dependent matrix adjusts the resulting weights, and the entire mechanism is learned end to end.

The added flexibility comes without increasing the rank of the adaptation weights. The approach therefore explores finer control within the low-rank structure rather than relying on a larger rank. Experiments across multiple models and datasets report consistent improvements over LoRA and its variants. Those findings support token-dependent projections as a useful way to improve parameter-efficient adaptation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-beyond-higher-rank-token-wi.tldr: TopLoRA improves low-rank adaptation by adjusting its projection for each token without increasing the adaptation rank.

paragraphs: DeCaFlow addresses causal inference when some variables that influence the system are hidden. It trains once on a dataset using observational measurements and the underlying causal graph, then supports causal questions involving continuous variables. The graph is part of the supplied information, so the method's setting includes knowledge of the causal structure.

The authors extend theoretical results on hidden confounding to show that one trained DeCaFlow instance correctly estimates all queries identifiable through do-calculus. They also use proxy variables to adjust causal effects where do-calculus alone is insufficient. For counterfactual questions, they establish identifiability when the corresponding interventional questions are identifiable.

These results connect the model's estimation claims to whether the desired causal quantity can be determined in the first place. Experiments across diverse settings report improvements over existing approaches. One evaluation uses Ecoli70 with three independent hidden confounders, tens of observed variables, and hundreds of causal queries, illustrating the framework's use across many questions within a single causal system.
neurips-2025-decaflow-a-deconfounding-ca.tldr: DeCaFlow trains once from observational data and a causal graph to answer identifiable causal and counterfactual questions under hidden confounding.

paragraphs: Pipeline parallelism spreads a language model's layers across devices so different stages can execute concurrently. Equal numbers of layers do not necessarily mean equal amounts of work, however. The final stage also performs operations such as sampling, making it slower and leaving earlier stages idle while they wait.

DynaPipe addresses this imbalance by predicting execution latency in real time and redistributing layers accordingly. Its balancing decision therefore reflects the work performed by each stage rather than simply counting layers. An asynchronous coordinator migrates the associated key-value cache, enabling layer redistribution without blocking inference.

Experiments on representative language models and diverse workloads report reductions of 8% to 49% in average end-to-end request latency compared with state-of-the-art pipeline parallelism systems. The results support accounting for post-processing when dividing inference work. They also show why moving layers requires coordinating the cached information they use: adaptive placement must remain practical while requests are already being served.
neurips-2025-dynapipe-dynamic-layer-redi.tldr: DynaPipe predicts stage latency and redistributes model layers during inference to reduce pipeline imbalance and request latency.

paragraphs: Language models generate outputs sequentially, which contributes to slow and expensive inference. EAGLE accelerates this process through speculative sampling that reuses features from the target model. The authors find, however, that increasing its training data brings limited improvement because its feature-prediction requirements constrain what the draft model can learn.

EAGLE-3 changes the draft model's objective to direct token prediction. It also combines features from multiple layers instead of relying only on the target model's top layer, using a technique called training-time test. Together, these changes improve performance and allow the draft model to benefit more effectively from additional training data.

The evaluation includes chat and reasoning models across five tasks. EAGLE-3 achieves speedups of up to 6.5 times, with about a 1.4-fold improvement over EAGLE-2. In SGLang, it improves throughput by 1.38 times at a batch size of 64. These results show acceleration in the tested settings, including a reported throughput benefit when serving larger batches.
neurips-2025-eagle-3-scaling-up-inferenc.tldr: EAGLE-3 combines direct token prediction with features from multiple layers to improve speculative inference and benefit from more training data.

paragraphs: When graph classes have very different numbers of nodes, learning to classify the minority classes becomes difficult. This paper examines that problem in semi-supervised classification, where labels are available for only part of the graph. Its focus is how passing information between connected nodes affects the geometry of the learned representations.

The authors introduce geometric imbalance to describe the ambiguity that message passing creates among minority-class nodes in a Riemannian manifold embedding space. This connects unequal class representation to the structure of the space in which nodes are represented. They provide a theoretical analysis of the phenomenon and design a framework intended to mitigate it explicitly.

The framework combines pseudo-label alignment, node reordering, and ambiguity filtering. Across diverse benchmark experiments, it consistently outperforms existing methods, with particularly strong results under severe class imbalance. The contribution is both explanatory and practical: it identifies a geometric consequence of imbalance and uses that analysis to guide a method for more robust node classification.
neurips-2025-geometric-imbalance-in-semi.tldr: The paper characterizes geometric ambiguity affecting minority graph classes and introduces a framework that improves classification under imbalance.

paragraphs: Different outdoor locations can have similar geometric shapes, making them difficult to distinguish from LiDAR measurements alone. GTR-Loc addresses this ambiguity by using textual descriptions as an additional source of localization guidance. The aim is to enrich what the model learns about a place beyond its point-cloud geometry.

A Geospatial Text Generator produces discrete descriptions that account for pose. A second module refines the text embeddings into view-specific representations conditioned on the current LiDAR features. These embeddings regularize localization learning, helping the model reduce confusion between geometrically similar locations.

The method then transfers textual knowledge through Modality Reduction Distillation, allowing inference to use LiDAR alone without generating text at runtime. Evaluations on QEOxford, Oxford Radar RobotCar, and NCLT show improvements over state-of-the-art approaches. On QEOxford, the reported gains are 9.64% in position accuracy and 8.04% in orientation accuracy. The results support using text during learning while retaining a LiDAR-only localization process at deployment.
neurips-2025-gtr-loc-geospatial-text-reg.tldr: GTR-Loc uses geospatial text to improve LiDAR localization during learning, then distills that knowledge for LiDAR-only inference.

paragraphs: Infographic charts communicate through icons, pictograms, and other deliberate design choices as well as numerical data. Understanding them requires recognizing those elements and reasoning about their meaning. InfoChartQA evaluates this combination, addressing gaps in existing chart-question benchmarks that lack matched plain charts and questions focused on visual design.

The benchmark contains 5,642 pairs of infographic and plain charts. Each pair presents the same underlying data in different visual forms. This pairing helps separate difficulty associated with the information itself from difficulty introduced by its presentation. Additional questions target the distinctive visual elements and the communicative intent behind them.

An evaluation of 20 multimodal language models finds a substantial performance decline on infographic charts. Questions involving visual metaphors are especially challenging. Because the benchmark holds the data constant within each pair, it supports detailed error analysis and ablation studies. The findings identify infographic design interpretation as an important obstacle beyond extracting values from conventional charts.
neurips-2025-infochartqa-a-benchmark-for.tldr: InfoChartQA pairs infographic and plain charts to reveal difficulties multimodal models face with visual design and metaphors.

paragraphs: Producing a good response and producing a response of the requested length are separate requirements. LIFEBench focuses on the latter, testing whether language models follow explicit length instructions. The motivation is that models may produce much shorter answers, stop early, or refuse requests even when they can handle demanding reasoning tasks.

The benchmark includes 10,800 instances across four task categories in English and Chinese. Its main length requirements range from 16 to 8,192 words, with additional evaluations extending to 32,000 words. This range lets the authors examine how adherence changes as requested outputs grow longer.

Across 26 models, most handle short-length instructions reasonably but deteriorate sharply beyond a threshold. Almost all fail to reach their vendor-claimed maximum output lengths in practice. Extended context windows do not improve length following in these evaluations, while reasoning models outperform even specialized long-text generation models. The findings distinguish the capacity to accommodate long sequences from the ability to generate a requested amount of text.
neurips-2025-lifebench-evaluating-length.tldr: LIFEBench finds that language models struggle to satisfy long output-length instructions, even when they support extended context windows.

paragraphs: This paper studies how normalization changes token representations as they pass through a deep transformer. Its focus is the evolution of those representations across layers, including whether they cluster together or collapse toward similar states. That perspective makes normalization part of the dynamics of representation learning.

The authors model tokens as interacting particles moving on a sphere. Within this mathematical description, normalization regulates the speed of their evolution. This provides a common language for examining several schemes: Post-LN, Pre-LN, Mix-LN, Peri-LN, nGPT, and LN-scaling. The same framework connects these choices to clustering behavior and representation collapse.

The analysis supplies a principled way to compare normalization schemes through their effects on token dynamics. It identifies Peri-LN as a particularly effective choice within that framework. The contribution is an explanatory connection between normalization and the way representations develop through depth, helping make architectural differences interpretable in terms of a shared mechanism of speed regulation.
neurips-2025-normalization-in-attention-.tldr: A particle-based analysis interprets transformer normalization as speed regulation and identifies Peri-LN as particularly effective within its framework.

paragraphs: Intermediate reasoning can improve language-model performance, but generated reasoning or programs can still produce undesirable solutions, particularly on algorithmic tasks. Per-Instance Program Synthesis addresses this by constructing and refining a program for the particular input being solved. The refinement uses structural feedback without requiring task-specific guidance or explicit test cases.

PIPS also includes a confidence measure that chooses between answering directly and using program synthesis for each instance. This makes the use of generated programs adaptive to the input. The method combines a refinement process with a decision about when that process should be used.

Experiments span three frontier language models and 30 benchmarks, covering difficult general reasoning, visual questions, relational reasoning, and mathematics. The reported absolute harmonic mean accuracy gains reach 8.6% over Program of Thought and 9.4% over Chain of Thought. On algorithmic tasks with Gemini-2.0-Flash, undesirable program generations fall by 65.1% relative to Program of Thought. These results support both improved accuracy and better program behavior in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-once-upon-an-input-reasonin.tldr: PIPS adaptively generates and refines programs for individual inputs, improving reasoning accuracy and reducing undesirable program outputs.

paragraphs: Representation alignment speeds up early diffusion-transformer training by matching hidden features to those of a non-generative teacher. This paper finds that continued alignment can later stall or degrade performance. The authors attribute the problem to a capacity mismatch: the teacher's representations eventually constrain the student's development as a generative model.

HASTE addresses this with two training phases. First, it aligns both attention maps and feature projections in the student's middle layers, transferring relational and semantic information. Then it switches off the alignment loss once a trigger, such as a fixed iteration, is reached. Subsequent training lets the model focus on denoising without the continuing teacher constraint.

The method requires no architecture changes. On ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution, it reaches the vanilla SiT-XL/2 baseline FID in 50 epochs and REPA's best FID in 500 epochs, with a reported 28-fold reduction in optimization steps. Improvements also extend to text-to-image models on MS-COCO, supporting the value of limiting alignment to a useful training phase.
neurips-2025-repa-works-until-it-doesnt-.tldr: HASTE accelerates diffusion training by aligning features and attention early, then removing the alignment constraint later.

paragraphs: Adversarial optimization searches for weaknesses in agents' policies, but applying it naively to cooperative tasks can encourage self-sabotage. Agents may block task completion, preventing useful learning from continuing. This paper develops a way to retain the benefits of adversarial search while avoiding that failure mode.

Rationality-preserving Policy Optimization requires agents to remain rational in a specific sense: each policy must be optimal for some possible partner policy. The authors develop Rational Policy Gradient to solve this formulation. It trains agents to maximize their own rewards in a modified game, using opponent shaping to optimize the adversarial objective.

This construction allows a range of existing adversarial optimization methods to be extended beyond the self-sabotaging behavior described in the paper. The resulting methods can find adversarial examples, improve robustness and adaptability, and learn diverse policies. Evaluations in several cooperative and general-sum environments report strong performance, supporting rationality preservation as a useful constraint when searching for challenging interactions between agents.
neurips-2025-robust-and-diverse-multi-ag.tldr: Rational Policy Gradient supports adversarial multi-agent learning while constraining agents to avoid self-sabotaging policies.

paragraphs: This paper proposes watermarks for DNA generated by language models, aiming to support accountability as sequence-design capabilities expand. It introduces two methods with different detection goals: marking DNA itself and creating a mark that remains detectable after the DNA is translated into a protein.

DNAMark embeds its signal through synonymous codon substitutions while preserving the function of the encoded proteins. CentralMark uses protein embeddings to make the watermark inheritable across translation from DNA to protein. Both methods use embeddings to generate watermark logits, with the aim of maintaining detection under mutations, synthesis errors, and adversarial attacks.

On a therapeutic DNA benchmark, both methods achieve detection F1 scores above 0.85 under diverse conditions. They also maintain more than 60% sequence similarity to ground truth and degeneracy scores below 15%. A CRISPR-Cas9 case study further illustrates CentralMark's application in synthetic biology. The contribution is a watermarking framework that connects traceability across DNA and protein representations while reporting sequence-preservation measures alongside detection performance.
neurips-2025-securing-the-language-of-li.tldr: DNAMark and CentralMark watermark generated DNA, with CentralMark extending detection to the translated proteins.

paragraphs: Inequality problems demand more than a plausible final answer: a solution must justify bounds and apply theorems correctly. This paper introduces IneqMath to evaluate those abilities using expert-curated Olympiad-level inequalities. Its formulation retains informal mathematical reasoning while making bound estimation and relation prediction automatically checkable.

The dataset includes a test set and a training corpus with step-by-step solutions and theorem annotations. The evaluation suite combines a final-answer judge with four specialized language-model judges that inspect common flaws in individual reasoning steps. This separates answer agreement from the quality of the deductive chain.

Across 29 leading models, even top systems such as o1 achieve less than 10% overall accuracy under step-wise scrutiny. The reported drop from final-answer-only evaluation reaches 65.5%. Larger models and more test-time computation yield limited gains in proof correctness. The findings expose a gap between reaching the right result and supporting it rigorously, while identifying theorem-guided reasoning and self-refinement as promising research directions.
neurips-2025-solving-inequality-proofs-w.tldr: IneqMath reveals a large gap between correct inequality answers and sound step-by-step proofs in leading language models.

paragraphs: Powerful image generators offer useful prior knowledge for reconstructing images from degraded observations. Applying that knowledge is difficult when the likelihood is intractable, the generator cannot directly accept the observations as conditioning, or its output departs from the measured data. FLAIR addresses these obstacles with a training-free variational framework for flow-based generators.

The method introduces a flow-matching objective that does not depend on a particular degradation type. Deterministic trajectory adjustments guide generation toward regions more likely under the posterior, combining the observations with the prior. FLAIR separates data-fidelity optimization from regularization to enforce exact consistency with the observed data.

A time-dependent calibration scheme also adjusts regularization strength using offline estimates of accuracy. This controls how strongly the generative prior influences reconstruction over time. On standard imaging benchmarks, FLAIR consistently outperforms existing diffusion- and flow-based methods in reconstruction quality and sample diversity. The findings support coordinating prior guidance with explicit observation consistency when adapting generative models to inverse imaging problems.
neurips-2025-solving-inverse-problems-wi.tldr: FLAIR uses flow-based image generators for training-free reconstruction while enforcing consistency with observed data.

paragraphs: Text-guided diffusion models can introduce incorrect details when enlarging an image. Their text descriptions may be incomplete or inaccurate, and cross-attention may connect those descriptions to irrelevant pixels. SRSR addresses both sources of semantic confusion by controlling where text influences the super-resolution process.

Its Spatially Re-focused Cross-Attention component uses visually grounded segmentation masks to guide attention at inference time. This ties text conditioning more closely to relevant image regions. A second component, Spatially Targeted Classifier-Free Guidance, selectively bypasses text influence on pixels that lack grounding, aiming to prevent unsupported details.

The framework is designed as a plug-and-play addition. Across synthetic and real-world datasets, it outperforms seven state-of-the-art baselines on the fidelity measures PSNR and SSIM. It also improves LPIPS and DISTS perceptual measures on two real-world benchmarks. These results support spatial control of text conditioning as a way to improve both semantic accuracy and visual quality, with the perceptual findings specifically established on those two benchmarks.
neurips-2025-srsr-enhancing-semantic-acc.tldr: SRSR grounds text guidance in image regions to reduce hallucinated details and improve diffusion-based super-resolution.

paragraphs: General-purpose models often perform best on common tasks and struggle with underrepresented uses. Adjusting prompts after training can be unpredictable because small wording changes may produce different behavior. This paper investigates training models to respond to explicit markers that give users more dependable ways to control generation.

The method builds a detailed taxonomy describing data characteristics and task provenance. These markers can explicitly control output attributes and implicitly condition generation at inference time. The base model is also fine-tuned to infer markers automatically, so users can omit them while still benefiting from the training approach.

The authors report an overall performance lift of 5.7% across tasks, with larger improvements for some long-tail uses. Relative gains reach 14.1% on underrepresented tasks such as CodeRepair, while length-instruction evaluations show absolute improvements of 35.3%. The results support building controllability into training as a way to help users target capabilities that ordinary training frequencies may leave less developed.
neurips-2025-treasure-hunt-real-time-tar.tldr: Training-time markers give users optional generation controls and improve performance on underrepresented tasks.

paragraphs: Reconstructing moving 3D scenes requires representing how many Gaussian elements deform over time. Existing approaches can be costly when they use dense neural networks or model every element independently. TreeSplat uses the observation that scene motion often has hierarchical structure and correlations between its parts.

The method organizes motion in a tree. Each node learns coefficients for time-varying basis functions, and a Gaussian's full motion accumulates transformations along its path from leaf to root. The tree grows adaptively during Gaussian densification: cloning or splitting a Gaussian also creates corresponding leaf nodes.

After training, the motion parameters along each Gaussian's path can be consolidated. This merging removes the need to traverse the tree during rendering, preserving the benefits of hierarchical learning without requiring that traversal at test time. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets report rendering above 200 frames per second, compact storage, and state-of-the-art rendering quality. The central contribution is a hierarchical motion representation that can be simplified efficiently for rendering.
neurips-2025-treesplat-mergeable-tree-fo.tldr: TreeSplat learns hierarchical Gaussian motion in a tree, then merges its parameters for fast, compact rendering.

paragraphs: Deep reinforcement learning can consume many training steps and require large experience replay buffers. This paper seeks to make better use of existing training information by retaining past outputs of the value network. These outputs are usually discarded, but the proposed method uses them to compute a causal bound.

The theoretical result draws on the Neyman-Rubin potential outcomes framework. It bounds factual loss, which the authors connect to on-policy loss in reinforcement learning, rather than focusing on counterfactual loss. Storing historical value-network outputs alongside replay experiences makes that bound available as an additional learning term.

Experiments cover Atari 2600 and MuJoCo using agents including DQN and SAC. Compared with the same agents without the proposed term, reported improvements reach a 383% higher reward ratio, while replay-buffer size reductions reach 96%. The authors describe the added cost as negligible. These results support recycling information already produced during training to improve sample efficiency and reduce storage requirements in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-turning-sand-to-gold-recycl.tldr: A causal loss bound reuses past value-network outputs to improve reinforcement-learning efficiency and reduce replay-buffer requirements.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action systems increasingly plan a task before generating actions, with reported improvements on complex, long-horizon manipulation. Comparing those approaches is difficult because their architectures, planning formats, and training data often differ simultaneously. VLA-OS provides a unified architecture suite to study planning choices while isolating them from architecture and data differences.

The controlled experiments cover rigid and deformable objects, 2D and 3D visual inputs, simulated and real environments, and both grippers and dexterous hands. This range lets the study examine planning representations and paradigms across varied manipulation settings rather than tying the comparison to a single type of robot interaction.

Two main findings emerge. Planning representations grounded in visual information generally outperform language-based representations. Hierarchical-VLA also generally performs better than the other paradigms, but requires slower training and inference. The study therefore offers evidence about which planning choices help and identifies a concrete speed tradeoff, while preserving that these are general tendencies in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-vla-os-structuring-and-diss.tldr: VLA-OS isolates planning choices and finds that visual grounding and hierarchical planning generally help, with hierarchical planning costing additional time.

paragraphs: Linear attention reduces the computational burden of processing long sequences, but distributing those sequences across devices can introduce substantial communication costs. ZeCO targets that bottleneck with a sequence-parallel method designed to keep end-to-end training close to linear scaling as sequence length and device count increase together.

Its core is All-Scan, a collective communication operation that gives each sequence-parallel rank precisely the initial operator state it needs. The operation minimizes the communication footprint, making overhead effectively negligible. The authors provide an optimality proof with negligible time and space overhead; the method still performs communication despite its zero-overhead name.

In one reported comparison, training a one-million-token sequence on 64 devices takes roughly as long as training a 16,000-token sequence on one device. At eight million tokens across 256 GPUs, ZeCO achieves a reported 60% speedup over the current state-of-the-art sequence-parallel method. The findings show how reducing communication overhead can make linear attention's computational advantages more useful in distributed training.
neurips-2025-zeco-zero-communication-ove.tldr: ZeCO minimizes sequence-parallel communication overhead to enable near-linear scaling for long-sequence training with linear attention.
